answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond that is slashed if its actions later prove fraudulent, while limiting influence until the account builds a history of independent, corroborated exchanges. A sybil operator must lock real capital in every identity and risk losing it, so multiplying fake accounts becomes costly rather than free. A whisper of coordinated behavior can trigger review; an opal-like trust score should not suffice alone, since one ripple of copied endorsements could otherwise validate an entire fake network.
